definition: In a symmetric run or walk cycle, a track whose value does not depend on left/right side - such as the hips' vertical (up-down) bob - only needs to be keyed for half the total cycle length; combined with the cycle's own left-right mirror symmetry and post/pre-infinity looping, that half automatically produces the correct motion for the full cycle, so the second half never needs to be keyed or matched by hand. A track that DOES depend on side (a forward/backward or side-to-side translation) is the explicit exception and must be keyed for the full cycle.
purpose: State a precise, almost mathematical shortcut for building a symmetric cycle's non-directional tracks, and name exactly which kind of track the shortcut does not apply to, rather than leaving 'cycles are symmetric' as a vague intuition.
visible_effect: A 7-frame-long vertical bob key range, once cycled, produces correct motion across the full 14-frame stride - deleting the second half of a hand-matched vertical curve and relying on the cycle produces an identical, perfectly consistent result to keying both halves by hand.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: None directly - a production-accuracy technique: it guarantees the two halves of a cycle's vertical motion are exactly consistent, which manual matching by eye cannot guarantee.
physical_interpretation: The vertical bob repeats once per STEP, not once per full stride (two steps), because gravity pulls the body down the same way regardless of which foot is leading - so its natural period is half the full left-right stride cycle.
use_cases: building the vertical (up-down) motion of a symmetric walk or run cycle's hips or root
identifying which tracks in a cycle qualify for this shortcut (non-directional, period-doubling ones) versus which do not (directional translation, which must span the full cycle)
non_use_cases: a directional track such as forward-progression or side-to-side sway, which the source explicitly excludes: "that doesn't work for things like the translate Z, because you're going from one side to another"
an intentionally asymmetric gait, where the two steps are not mirror images of each other and this shortcut's premise does not hold
interactions: symmetric_pose_mirroring_workflow (W03, video 27) - the same underlying mirror-symmetry assumption, applied here to a continuous curve's period rather than to a single key's value
walk_cycle_vertical_drop_is_arrested_fall (W03, video 26) - the vertical curve this technique halves is exactly that entry's single-peak-per-step drop
cadence_representation: Not built as an authoring shortcut, though the underlying pieces exist. The project's cycle/loop evaluation and mirror_item each exist independently; nothing currently offers 'key half a symmetric cycle's non-directional track and derive the rest' as one operation - a caller would have to key the half-cycle and rely on the project's own cycle/loop evaluation, which is a manual assembly of existing pieces, not a single built shortcut.
control_surface: None specific; mirror_item and the track evaluation's own looping are each independently available.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Not applicable directly - a generation/workflow shortcut rather than something to measure. A validation check IS possible: confirming a track's second half is an exact within-tolerance repeat of its first half (offset by the half-period) would verify the technique was applied correctly, using nothing beyond existing key-value comparison.
generation_or_modification_methods: Partly buildable from existing pieces (see cadence_representation); not implemented as a single operation.
failure_modes: hand-keying both halves of a vertical bob and letting them drift out of sync with each other, which this shortcut avoids by construction
applying the same half-cycle shortcut to a directional track, which the source explicitly warns does not work
roblox_considerations: None beyond the shared keyframe/cycling model.
performance_implications: Fewer authored keys for an equivalent result - a minor efficiency gain, not a runtime performance concern.
examples: "things like the up-down of the hips can just be half of a cycle and it will cycle for the entire run - if I cycle it for seven frames here, it will work for fourteen frames, the whole cycle... you can just delete half of this and it cycles perfectly" - video @ 20:41-21:22
the named exception: "obviously that doesn't work for things like the translate Z, because you're going from one side to another" - video @ 21:32-21:37
